Court Services

Fullerton Courthouse Extension

You can request an extension for citations and traffic school completion through the Clerk’s Office. The first extension allows an additional 45 days, while a second extension of 30 days may be granted if there’s no previous failure to appear or warrants. Payments can be made via credit card, with a service fee of $6.20.

Payment Options

To pay fines at Fullerton Court, you can choose from the following methods:

  1. In-Person: Visit the court during business hours.
  2. Telephone: Call 877-872-2122 for payment over the phone.
  3. Mail: Send a check to the court's mailing address at 1275 N. Berkeley Avenue, Fullerton, California 92832.

Case Access

You can access your case details in various ways:

  • By Person Name
  • By Business Name
  • By Case Number
  • By Filing Date
  • By Unlawful Detainer

Available Forms

Fullerton Court provides several types of forms to assist with legal processes:

  • Approved State Judicial Council Form: Statewide approved forms for all division cases.
  • Locally Approved Form: Local forms for all division cases.
  • Packet Form of Self-Help: Various packet forms and document reviews.

Fees

Fees at Fullerton Court vary depending on the case type:

  • Probate Fees: $200 for first administration without general representation.
  • Confession of Judgment Fee: $45.
  • Advance Jury Fee: $150.
  • Adoption Petition Fee: $20.
  • Blocked Account Withdrawal Funds Petition Fee: $60.
  • Conservator’s Information Package Fee: $20.

E-Filing

E-Filing allows electronic submission of cases. Once filed, documents receive a timestamp and confirmation receipt. All division cases can be e-filed, except certain civil probate cases.

Marriage Licenses

Marriage licenses are issued by the Family Law Division at Fullerton Court. Two types are available:

  • Public Marriage License: $61 fee, information accessible to anyone.
  • Confidential Marriage License: $66 fee, private information only available to the couple.

Filing for Divorce

Divorces are processed through the Family Law Division. You can hire a lawyer or represent yourself through self-help resources. The process typically takes at least six months, with grounds for divorce including irreconcilable differences and incurable insanity.
